newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end up on last-gasp portfolio buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end up on last-gasp portfolio buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended slightly up on Wednesday on last-minute buying for month-end portfolio valuation after drifting in negative turf for most of the session in pre-holiday doldrums, traders said.
"It was a quiet session ... Volume was thin, dead." said Roberto Campuzano, an equity analyst with the Invex brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 5.48 points, or 0.14 percent, at 3,842.94.
Trading volume was lackluster at 50.6 million shares.
"There were few dealers left at the end, they already sorted out who would stay and who would leave early," a floor trader added.
The Dow Jones meanwhile ended up 0.07 percent at 6,880.70 points.
Mexican financial markets are closed on Thursday and Friday, March 27 and 28, for Easter. Many in Mexico have been on vacation since another public holiday was celebrated last Friday, March 21.
"Nothing happened, interest was scant as most dealers are on vacation," a desk trader said.
"The U.S. rates hike had little effect as it had already been discounted," he added.
The Federal Open Market Committee decided to raise U.S. overnight federal funds rates by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent on Tuesday.
"We may see more buyers step in next week, because the bourse has stood up well to recent events," Campuzano added, referring to the FOMC decision.
"It should speed up on a favorable outlook for economic news," he said.
On the broad market, 98 shares changed hands, with gainers just outnumbering sliders by 35 to 34.
Telmex L class weighed most heavily on the session, accounting for 23 percent of all shares traded, and ended down two centavos at 15.66 pesos. Telmex ADRs, meanwhile, closed down 1/8 at 39-3/8.
Dealers said last-minute buyers pushed up prices of holding company Grupo Carso, Carso Global Telecom and construction firm ICA.
Grupo Carso gained 50 centavos to 47.50 pesos, Carso Global ended up 20 centavos at 24.50.
ICA, meanwhile, rose 1.10 pesos to 130.00 pesos.
Corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca was another prominent gainer, up 14 centavos to 8.34 pesos.
"People believe in Maseca and it was very cheap, but we don't think it has a full tank of gas. It gained on the price hike business," Rodolfo Campuzano said.

Radio network Radio Red said on Wednesday morning that the price ceiling for tortillas was to be raised by almost 50 percent, but the move was swiftly denied by the Mexican Trade Ministry. Traders said the decliners' list was headed by stocks that had moved on low volume.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
